name: Maonan
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

Text reached as scan highlight fragments from the Open Library search-inside API: (p. 154), (p. 105 + index line), (index 'stress: 154')
catalog_quote: Unlike languages like English and Mandarin Chinese, Maonan does not assign suprasegmental features to different syllables to differentiate compound words, word compound or phrases. For example, in Mandarin, the compound word déngxi with the second syllable unaccented, means ‘thing’, but the word compound déngxi, with both syllables stressed, means ‘east and west’, and in English, ‘blackbird’ [ ‘b/ekboad], with the stress on the first syllable, refers to a kind of bird with yellow bill, but ‘black bird’ | blek ba:d)|, with the stress on the second syllable, refers to any kind of birds that are black in colour. In Maonan, "da'/a:n’ (eye-red), with both syllables stressed, means either ‘jealous’ or ‘the eyes become red’. // p. 105 (§2.8.5 Suprafixation): Suprafixation here refers to the change or adding of suprasegmental features as a morphological operation (Payne 1997: 29-30). Maonan is a tonal language which distinguishes words by ‘tonemes’. Such use of suprasegmental features plays a significant role in Maonan lexicology

For example, in Mandarin, the compound word dōngxi with the second syllable unaccented, means ‘thing’, but the word compound dōngxi, with both syllables stressed, means ‘east and west’ [...]. In Maonan, ˀda¹ɬaːn¹ (eye-red), with both syllables stressed, means either ‘jealous’ or ‘the eyes become red’. // p. 105: Maonan is a tonal language which distinguishes words by ‘tonemes’. Such use of suprasegmental features plays a significant role in Maonan lexicology.

The 725-char quote in the NOTE is fully covered by overlapping fragments (olc_2.9, olc_14, olc_15, olc_17, olc_20, olb_1, olb_2, olb_16, olb_17, olb_27, olb_28, old_1, old_11, ole_5): 'Unlike languages like English and Mandarin Chinese, Maonan does not assign suprasegmental features to different syllables to differentiate compound words, word compound or…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Maonan is a tone language (8 tones plus a borrowed low-falling tone); the grammar contains no rule locating word stress. Its one statement on stress says that, unlike English or Mandarin, Maonan does not use differential stress (or other suprasegmental features) across the syllables of a word to distinguish compounds from phrases: in a disyllabic compound such as ˀda¹ɬaːn¹ 'eye-red' = 'jealous'/'eyes become red' both syllables are stressed (i.e. no unstressed/neutral-tone syllable, no culminative word stress). Stress is thus non-contrastive and effectively absent as a word-level parameter; tone and tone sandhi carry the lexical and morphological load (suprafixation).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for stress. Tone-related: tone sandhi occurs in the first or second syllable of compounds depending on the closeness of binding (pp. 104-105, Table 37), never in the final syllable; clause-final particles have 'weakened', unstable tones (p. 289); grammaticalised words are 'reduced in prominence' (ch. 7).
new_statements.domain_note: The statement concerns disyllabic compound words vs. phrases (word level). The passage was reconstructed from overlapping scanned highlight snippets returned by the Open Library search-inside API, not from a full page scan; scanned normalisations: 'déngxi' -> dōngxi, '"da'/a:n’' -> ˀda¹ɬaːn¹ (tone superscripts not legible in scanned). The elided '[..]' portion is the parallel English blackbird/black bird example.
new_statements.identity_note: Lu 2008 describes the Maonan of Huanjiang Maonan Autonomous County, Guangxi (author's native variety; Xianan/Huanjiang dialect area) — same languoid as maon1241; no dialect split needed. Coyaud 1987 and maonan.org describe the same standard variety (based on Liang Min 1980).

tone_statements.citation: 李钊祥 [Li Zhaoxiang]. 1982. 现代侗台语诸语言声调和韵尾的对应规律 [Correspondence rules of tones and rhyme codas among the modern Kam-Tai languages]. 民族语文 (Minzu Yuwen) 1982年第4期.
tone_statements.quote: 毛南语的声调分为两类：带塞音韵尾-p、-t、-k 的音节属促声调，其余都是舒声调。舒声调共有 6 个，即第 1、2、3、4、5、6 调。促声调有 2 个，即第 7 调和第 8 调。第 7、第 8 调又由于元音长短而在调值上存在细微的差别。 … 本文首先通过声学分析对毛南语的声调系统进行研究，经过归纳，得到毛南语 8 个单音节声调的五度值为：1 调-51，2 调-241，3 调-431，4 调-24，5 调-44，6 调-323，7 调-44，8 调-24。
tone_statements.translation: Maonan tones fall into two classes: syllables with stop codas -p, -t, -k carry checked tones, all others unchecked tones. There are 6 unchecked tones, tones 1-6, and 2 checked tones, tones 7 and 8; tones 7 and 8 further differ slightly in value with vowel length. … Through acoustic analysis of the Maonan tone system we obtain the five-degree values of the 8 monosyllabic tones: T1 51, T2 241, T3 431, T4 24, T5 44, T6 323, T7 44, T8 24.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.3 声调, p. 62 + sec. 6 总结, p. 72
tone_statements.summary: Eight tones: six on smooth syllables (51, 241, 431, 24, 44, 323), two on stop-final ones (44, 24); morae of a bimoraic rhyme bear tone; first-syllable sandhi, mostly via floating tones; downstep.
